subject: Post-call: Multilingual evals & next steps
messages:
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.ai>
To: Ana Müller <ana.muller@globex-eu.com>, Satoshi Tanaka <s.tanaka@kaizen.co.jp>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>

Subject: Post-call: Multilingual evals & next steps

Hi Ana / Satoshi —

Thanks again for the time today. Quick recap and proposed next steps based on our call: 

Summary of needs:
- Customer-facing product descriptions and returns flow in DE/FR/ES for EU storefronts
- Order status/chatbot experience (+ localized tone) for JP/KO in APAC pilot
- Low tolerance for hallucinations on legal/terms language; need precision on EU languages

Proposed technical approach:
1) Run targeted evals on your existing prompt sets + our recommended models (see attachments).
2) Prioritize French/German/Spanish benchmark slices first, then JP/KR.
3) If we see regressions vs your baseline, we’ll run prompt-tuning and compare quantization profiles.

Deliverables & timeline:
- Redwood will share an initial eval report (attached) by Friday 2026-02-14.
- We’ll provide a short prompt_samples.csv with locale-specific prompts for your team to review.
- Proposed follow-up: 30-min review on Mon 2026-02-16 (suggest 09:00 CET / 17:00 JST).

Recommended models to try (quick guidance):
- redwood-instruct-multilingual-v1 (cost-balanced for broad coverage; good for FR/ES)
- redwood-llama-70b-q4f (higher quality for DE legal text; use in dedicated run)
- open-llm-multilingual-13b-8bit (low-cost baseline for APAC JP/KR checks)

Benchmark links and attachments:
- Drive folder with per-locale benchmarks and the eval script: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3c-redwood-multilingual-evals
- Attached: redwood_multilingual_eval_report_v1.pdf and prompt_samples_globex.csv

Open questions I noted from the call:
- Ana: do you have a preferred baseline model or internal evaluation metric for hallucination tolerance?
- Satoshi: can your team provide 200 sample JP/KR utterances (support requests) by EOD Monday?

Next steps (action owners):
- Redwood: run the FR/DE/ES eval pass and surface any quality regressions (Vanessa).
- Globex: share JP/KR samples + any locale-specific safety rules (Ana/Satoshi).
- Sales ops: Marissa to confirm rough pricing estimate for dedicated runs after we validate QA.

Thanks — I’ll send the report on Friday and include clear pass/fail flags per locale.

—
Vanessa Ortiz
Enterprise AE | Redwood Inference

Thanks Vanessa — this looks good. A couple quick clarifications: 

1) Baseline & metrics: we currently use an internal precision metric and a human-rated correctness score (0-5) for critical legal copy. If you can map your pass/fail flags to those scales, that will help the legal team.
2) Timing: we can get JP/KR samples by Mon EOD (Satoshi is looped in).

Also: are you able to include a short check for GDPR-specific disclosures (FR/DE) in the report? Those are a hard stop for us.

Appreciate it — look forward to the report.

Date: Fri, 14 Feb 2026 07:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Post-call: Multilingual evals & next steps

Hi Ana — great, thanks for the quick reply and for outlining the baseline. A few notes after running the first pass (summary attached):

- Initial findings (high level):
  * FR/ES: redwood-instruct-multilingual-v1 matches your baseline on general product copy; small regressions on legal phrasing in FR (2 examples flagged).
  * DE: redwood-llama-70b-q4f shows higher correctness on formal/legal language but is 2.4x costlier on token compute; recommend targeted use for contracts/terms outputs.
  * JP/KR (baseline quick check): open-llm-multilingual-13b-8bit performs acceptably for conversational flows but struggles on honorifics/keigo in some JP samples.

- GDPR check: we added locale-specific prompts to validate disclosure language in FR/DE — see flagged items in the attached PDF. We can run an expanded legal pass if you want stricter gating.

Attachments included: redwood_multilingual_eval_report_v1.pdf (summary + per-locale flags), prompt_samples_globex.csv (sample prompts and instructions).

Proposed next steps:
- If Globex wants higher precision on DE legal copy, we recommend a two-track approach: run a dedicated DE-focused pass on redwood-llama-70b with stricter generation constraints + human review workflow. Estimated turnaround: 5 business days after approval.
- For JP honorifics, we can try prompt variants and a small in-context-tuning run (100-500 examples) to reduce keigo errors.

Marissa / Neha — can you confirm a ballpark for a single dedicated DE run (70b) and the pricing/commit guidelines so I can propose internally?

Ana/Satoshi — can you join a quick 30-min review Monday? I penciled 09:00 CET / 17:00 JST. Marissa will follow up with calendar invite once pricing is confirmed.

Thanks,
Vanessa
